title: 出其东门
author: 佚名（《诗经·郑风》）
authorEn: Anonymous (Book of Songs, Airs of Zheng)
intro: Outside the city gate the girls are as many as clouds — but the young man only has eyes for one, in a plain white dress. The source of the idiom 美女如云, and one of the oldest poems about faithful love.
analysis: 城东门外，出游的姑娘多得像天上的云、像满地的白茅花。可是男子说：她们虽然多，却都不是我心里想的那一个。我想的只是那个穿着白绢衣服、戴着青灰色（或浅红色）头巾的姑娘——她穿得朴素，大概家境也一般，可只有她能让我快乐。诗用“如云”“如荼”写姑娘之多、之美，然后一句“匪我思存”把这一切都推开，用众多来衬托唯一，这种手法叫“衬托”。两章结构相同，只换了几个字，是民歌常见的“重章叠句”。今天形容美女很多的成语“美女如云”就和这首诗有关。古往今来，人们用它来赞美专一的爱情：世界再大、选择再多，心里只有一个人。
analysisEn: Outside the east gate of the city, crowds of young women are out enjoying the day — as many as clouds in the sky, as thick as white reed flowers. But the young man says: there are so many, yet none is the one my heart is set on. The one he wants wears a plain white silk dress and a grey-green (in the second stanza, a rose-red) headscarf — simple clothes, perhaps a girl from an ordinary family — and only she can make him happy. The poem first piles up the crowd with two vivid comparisons, 如云 and 如荼, then sweeps them all aside with one phrase, 匪我思存, “not the one I think of”. Using the many to set off the one is a technique called 衬托 (contrast that highlights). Like many folk songs, the two stanzas repeat the same frame with a few words changed. The idiom 美女如云, “beautiful women as many as clouds”, is linked to this poem. Readers have long loved it as a picture of single-hearted love: however many choices there are, there is only one person for him.
background: The Book of Songs gathers 305 songs from roughly the 11th to the 6th century BC. The “Airs of Zheng” (郑风) are famous for their love songs; the east gate of the Zheng capital (in present-day Henan) is said to have been a popular place for spring outings.
pronunciation: 綦 qí；员 yún（语气词）；闉阇 yīn dū；荼 tú；茹藘 rú lǘ；匪 fěi；缟 gǎo；聊乐 lè。“匪我思且”的“且”：按旧注读 jū（语气词），也有注本读 cú（通“徂”），当前采用 jū。
version: 采用通行的《毛诗》文本，全诗两章，每章六句，网站按两个四字句为一行排版（共六行）。

lines.py: chū qí dōng mén, yǒu nǚ rú yún
lines.lit: I go out of the east gate: there are girls like clouds.
lines.en: Out through the east gate — girls everywhere, as many as clouds.

lines.py: suī zé rú yún, fěi wǒ sī cún
lines.lit: Although they are like clouds, none is the one my thoughts dwell on.
lines.en: So many, like clouds — but none of them is the one I think about.

lines.py: gǎo yī qí jīn, liáo lè wǒ yún
lines.lit: White silk dress, grey-green scarf — she alone gives me joy.
lines.en: Only the girl in the plain white dress and grey-green scarf can make me happy.

lines.py: chū qí yīn dū, yǒu nǚ rú tú
lines.lit: I go out through the outer gate: there are girls like reed flowers.
lines.en: Out past the gate tower — girls everywhere, like white reed flowers.

lines.py: suī zé rú tú, fěi wǒ sī jū
lines.lit: Although they are like reed flowers, none is the one I long for.
lines.en: So many, like flowers — but none of them is the one I want.

lines.py: gǎo yī rú lǘ, liáo kě yǔ yú
lines.lit: White silk dress, madder-red scarf — with her I could be happy.
lines.en: Only the girl in the plain white dress and rose-red scarf — with her I’d be glad.

words.note: 今天说“美女如云”“高手如云”。
通“非”；今天“匪”多指强盗（土匪）。

words.en: a dress of plain white silk
words.note: 缟：白色的生绢，朴素的衣料。
古义“姑且、只是”；今天“聊天”的“聊”是谈话。
语气词，同“云”，没有实际意思。

words.en: the outer gate tower of a city wall
white flowers of reeds or cogon grass
words.note: 成语“如火如荼”的“荼”，原指白茅花。

words.en: madder, a plant used for red dye (here, a red scarf)

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: “有女如云”：姑娘多得像天上的云，用来衬托他只爱一个人。
imagery.en: Girls as many as clouds — the crowd that makes his love for just one stand out.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: “有女如荼”：姑娘们像遍地的白茅花一样多、一样美，可都不是他想要的。
imagery.en: Girls like a field of white reed flowers — lovely and countless, yet none is the one he wants.
